items: correctness-1: One per-install presentation profile (language, register, audience) is the single source of truth for the install; it is per-install state written by install/sync, never repo content in the claude-configs repo.

correctness-2: The profile is materialized under ~/.claude/context/global/ so the global-context hook injects it into every session on the machine — interactive Claude sessions and smine skill runs alike.

correctness-3: The profile names and supersedes the global 'handoff/doc artifacts always English' rule for end-user-visible artifacts only; repo content, logs, results.jsonl and other operator artifacts stay English.

correctness-4: All user-visible prose produced by the smine pipeline (proposal titles, change lines, detail fields, evidence notes, group titles, batch report views) is in the profile language, semi-casual/semi-professional, backed by a jargon glossary of banned engine/developer terms (worktree, ACDSL gate, transcript mining, consolidate) with plain replacements.

correctness-5: The nightly consolidate stage is invoked with `language <lang>` and acts as the drift-correction gate rewriting English/jargon prose in the proposal store; snippets[].code, ids, dates, tags and gate fields are never translated or reworded.

correctness-6: The config-server UI gets a German message overlay (English stays default and fallback) covering the pages the casual user sees, and the `<html lang>` attribute is driven by the profile instead of the hardcoded `en`.

correctness-7: For the casual audience, engine-internal navigation tabs (Skills, Context, Tools, Checklist, Config and similar developer surfaces) are not shown, and proposal cards hide gate band, tags and target internals while code snippets render collapsed, marked as technical detail and untranslated.

correctness-8: Audience gating is a render-time filter over the same data (no forked handlers); switching the profile back to developer/English restores the full UI and English register for the operator.
correctness-9: A casual German user sees proposal titles, change lines and detail fields in plain German, and evidence notes phrased as everyday explanations of what happened in their sessions.
correctness-10: Engine terms (worktree, gate, transcript mining, consolidation) never appear in text the casual user reads.
correctness-11: Navigation and page headings render in German for the casual German user.
correctness-12: The casual user sees only pages relevant to them, not internals such as skills, context packs or repo-management machinery.
correctness-13: Proposal cards for the casual user show no gate bands, tags or target paths — only what is suggested and why.
correctness-14: Nightly runs keep user-visible content German and jargon-free so English developer prose does not leak in over time.
correctness-15: Technical code blocks are visibly marked as technical detail and left untranslated.

correctness-16: The operator sets the presentation profile once at install, can switch a machine back to developer/English mode for the full UI and register, and repo content, logs and pipeline results stay English regardless of the profile.

correctness-17: Template `settings/claude_code/presentation-profile.de.md` exists with `---` front matter `language: de` plus the casual audience value and a German directive body: all user-visible prose in German, semi-casual register, banned-term glossary with plain-German replacements, never translate code blocks/identifiers/ids/dates/tags/file paths/snippets, technical fragments collapsed and labeled 'Technisches Detail'.

correctness-18: `cmd/hooks/global-context.sh` scans `$HOME/.claude/context/global/*.md` before the repo-local `$DOCS_DIR/global/*.md`, emitting the unchanged GLOBAL CONTEXT header once and one `===== <file> =====` block per file, under the existing GLOBAL_CONTEXT_ENABLED kill switch; shellcheck-clean and bash-3.2 compatible.

correctness-19: `loadPresentationProfile(path)` parses `language:`/`audience:` from the first `---` front-matter block and fails open: missing/unreadable file, no front matter or missing keys yield language `en` and developer audience; an empty language becomes `en`; any audience other than the casual value counts as developer.

correctness-20: configserver gains a `-presentation` flag defaulting to the exported `server.DefaultPresentationPath()` (~/.claude/context/global/presentation-profile.md), threaded into `Options.PresentationPath`; a zero value means defaults.

correctness-21: The template FuncMap gains `t` (translate via `germanCatalog` keyed by the English source string; identity when the language is not `de` or the key is missing), a lang-attribute func feeding `<html lang=...>`, and `isDeveloperAudience`; templates referencing them parse in `New`.

correctness-22: Layout nav wraps the Overview/Sessions/Proposals labels in `t` and renders Config, Skills, Context, Repos, Routines, Tools, Checklist and Peek only for the developer audience; direct URLs to hidden pages stay reachable.
correctness-23: `handleOverview` for the casual audience appends only `sessionTiles` and `proposalsTile` with a translated title; overview tile labels render through `{{t .Label}}`.

correctness-24: `_proposal_card.html` renders the target badge, gate band badge, tag badges and the gate detail row only for the developer audience; for casual the snippet summary becomes `t "technical detail"` (Technisches Detail) while the code stays untranslated; the comment placeholder, postpone button, details/fields/evidence summary and static texts of proposals/sessions templates are wrapped in `t`.

correctness-25: `routines/smine-nightly/run.sh` reads `language:` from ~/.claude/context/global/presentation-profile.md with sed; when set and not `en` the consolidate prompt becomes `/smine-consolidate proposals language <lang>`, otherwise it stays `/smine-consolidate proposals`.
correctness-26: With no profile file the UI stays English with `lang="en"`, the full developer nav and overview tiles, and the consolidate prompt carries no language arg.

correctness-27: `install.sh` copies `settings/claude_code/presentation-profile.${SMINE_PRESENTATION_PROFILE}.md` to ~/.claude/context/global/presentation-profile.md (mkdir -p) only when `SMINE_PRESENTATION_PROFILE` is set; a default install plants no profile.

correctness-28: Windows installer: smine.iss adds a `TInputOptionWizardPage` after RepoPage with 'Default — English, developer' checked and a German casual option; a `ProfileArg` [Code] function appends ` -presentation-profile=de` to the `[Run]` `-install` parameters; install.ps1 gains a matching `-PresentationProfile` parameter forwarded as `-presentation-profile=`.

correctness-29: The configserver `-presentation-profile` flag is passed into `runInstall` (Windows and the non-Windows stub); after successful syncs `installPresentationProfile` copies the repo template to %USERPROFILE%\.claude\context\global\presentation-profile.md (creating the dir), an empty id installs nothing, and errors follow the file's existing error style.

correctness-30: The `settings/claude_code/CLAUDE.md` artifact-language rule gains the supersede clause: an installed presentation profile overrides the always-English rule for end-user-visible artifacts; code, logs, commits and repo docs stay English.

correctness-31: proposals.html renders the kind heading as `{{t .File.Kind}}`, category/group/subgroup titles as `{{t .Title}}`, and wraps the literals 'updated', 'Everything applied, happy' and 'file(s) failed to load:' in `t`; free-form and path titles fall back to identity.

correctness-32: proposals.go vote tooltips are built with `fmt.Sprintf(translate(s.profile.Language, <format key>), ...)` using format-string keys ('%d of %d accepted', '%d rejected', '%d postponed'); category names stay untouched Go keys translated via the section-title `t`.

correctness-33: Remaining Go-composed casual-visible overview strings (signalDetail fragments, the '%+d vs batch %d' delta) go through `translate`, and the overview window filter labels render through `{{t .Label}}`.

correctness-34: germanCatalog gains entries byte-exact to the rendered keys: 'New skills'→'Neue Funktionen', 'Edits to existing skills'→'Änderungen an bestehenden Funktionen', 'Workflows (skill-bundled scripts)'→'Abläufe (gebündelte Skripte)', 'Considered, not proposed'→'Geprüft, nicht vorgeschlagen', the context/routines/rules/actions/facts/acdsl kind and category names, 'updated', the empty-state and load-error strings, and the tooltip/delta format strings.
correctness-35: Canonical skills-group titles stay verbatim English in the proposals JSON (smine-apply routes on 'Workflows (skill-bundled scripts)') and are translated only at render time.

correctness-36: smine-batch, smine-skills, smine-routines, smine-context and smine-memory SKILL.md each gain a Language contract: read ~/.claude/context/global/presentation-profile.md; when `language:` is set and not `en`, author the skill's user-visible prose fields in that language following the profile register/glossary; never translate ids, targets, paths, code, dates, tags, schema keys, status values or fixed group titles; absent profile = English; each skill bumps its frontmatter version and changelog.json[0].

correctness-37: smine-batch's language field list covers the sessions-JSON prose (batch title, theme bullets, arc summaries, session summaries/notes, finding titles) while its `.md` report stays English; smine-skills flags its mandated group titles as verbatim keys; smine-context/smine-memory group titles (target-surface paths) are never translated.

correctness-38: smine-consolidate `language <lang>` becomes a full sweep: every user-visible prose field (title change-name part, change, fields, evidence titles, session notes, free-form group titles) of every mutable entry not already in <lang> is translated in place; fixed structural group titles and identifiers stay verbatim; voted/immutable entries are untouched; the grouping invariant and §4 Presentation are amended; version bumped.
correctness-39: Machines without a profile keep English proposal titles and tooltips unchanged, and the proposals/sessions schema is not changed.
correctness-40: The rollout note documents a one-time `/smine-consolidate proposals language de` run (or the next nightly) to translate the already-seeded store; no migration code is added.

correctness-41: The sync_hooks.sh prune prompt uses `read -r answer || answer=n` so EOF/no stdin answers no and never aborts the install under `set -euo pipefail`; pruning still requires an explicit yes.

correctness-42: `shell.RunSync` with `SyncTimeout = 10 * time.Minute` mirrors RunDialog (platformArgv, HideWindow, WaitDelay, shell log line, wrapped error); all four sync-script call sites (install_windows.go x2, contextdocs/sync.go, skills/sync.go) use it and no `shell.Run` call on sync_* or ensure_git_repo remains.

correctness-43: On a casual profile sync_skills.sh jq-merges `skillOverrides: {<leaf>: "off"}` for every deployed leaf into ~/.claude/settings.json preserving foreign keys and non-leaf overrides, writes the overlay ~/.config/claude-routine/skill-overrides.json with the same leaves `"on"`, and merges that overlay into the repo's gitignored `.claude/settings.local.json`; on a developer profile it deletes the overlay and drops the leaf overrides (idempotent flip).

correctness-44: Routine runs copy the skill overlay into each routine worktree's `.claude/settings.local.json` (gitignored, never committed by publish); no `--settings` overlay injection is added to `routine_run_claude`.

correctness-45: The repos page for the casual audience renders as Projects/Projekte: `t`-localized add/remove forms kept, the `additional-dir` checkbox hidden, the table showing only the name/label (rows not linked to repo management); the casual nav gains a `{{t "Projects"}}` link to /repos after Proposals; every route stays reachable for all audiences.
correctness-46: `handleReposAdd` grants additionalDirectories when the checkbox is on OR the audience is casual; a developer add without the checkbox leaves permissions unchanged.

correctness-47: `Repo` gains optional `Label` (`json:"label,omitempty"`, at most 80 chars, display-only; Name stays the URL/dedup key); the add form has a label input for both audiences; Projekte rows and the developer Name column show the label falling back to the name; i18n entries cover Projects/add/remove/label/confirm/empty-state strings.

correctness-48: Adding a folder without `.git` (dir or file) runs `git init -b main` there via internal/shell before `registry.Add`, never configures a remote, and an init failure fails the add; folders that already have `.git` are untouched.

correctness-49: New `smine-orchestrate` skill (+ changelog.json; argument-hint `<branch> | bootstrap`; manifest with Read/Write/Edit and git/jq/make audit/acdsl/sync Bash tools): branch mode judges main..<branch> (schema-valid JSON, make audit green, prose vs the profile, re-judges auto-applied changes reverting bad ones and marking the proposal rejected), fixes small defects or rejects with the reason in `.orchestrate-report`, merges into main and re-audits (red reverts and rejects), runs sync_settings/hooks/skills, re-syncs context packs per registered repo with recorded options (per-repo failures non-fatal), appends missing registry paths to additionalDirectories (never removes), pushes only when a remote exists, and reports one line per duty; bootstrap mode judges the working tree with initial-setup framing and commits directly without a branch/merge.

correctness-50: run.sh parses `audience:` above stage 1; `ROUTINE_ORCHESTRATE` defaults on and `SMINE_AUTO_APPLY` defaults to `decide` for the casual audience (env values win); developer machines get no stage 3 and keep apply default never.

correctness-51: Stage 3 runs only when exit and publish status are 0, from the main checkout with `/smine-orchestrate <run_branch>`, manifest `--allowedTools`, ROUTINE_MODEL default, `--effort medium`, permission mode/budget/JSON output like the consolidate stage; postconditions: a dirty repo_root tree marks failure (70), a branch that is an ancestor of main triggers `routine_prune_merged`, otherwise the kept branch is logged and `.orchestrate-report` tailed; the report file is always removed; a non-zero stage status propagates to the run exit status.

correctness-52: The Welcome Bootstrap card mirrors the verify-token control (hx-post `/welcome/bootstrap`, hx-confirm, indicator); the handler refuses a second concurrent run with a conflict response, spawns the bootstrap detached with output to a log file and a logged pid, and responds started; `GET /welcome/bootstrap/status` resolves the newest running session via the peek client and renders the session id + peek link, else 'starting…'; both routes registered next to the welcome routes.
correctness-53: The Welcome nav entry gating reverts to plain `{{if initWelcome}}` (no audience condition).
correctness-54: The Windows folder-picker fix follows captured evidence: the picker's owner form is shown and activated so the dialog opens in front instead of behind; no speculative rewrite.

correctness-55: New `acdsl/policy.json` (mode free, dist_mode gated, base_ref '', editable_scopes GOLANG/PYTHON/SHELL/SQL/JSON, empty verifier_allowlist and local_overrides, allow_task_contracts true) and draft-07 `acdsl/policy.schema.json` (required mode; mode/dist_mode enum free|gated|strict; scope pattern ^[A-Z]{2,12}$; additionalProperties false), gated by new rule ACDSL-JSON-003 (jsonschema, reach global, empty ok, needs the schema) with a pass fixture and fail fixtures for a bad mode and an unknown key.

correctness-56: `LoadPolicy(root)`: an absent file yields free mode with AllowTaskContracts true; an absent `allow_task_contracts` key keeps true; malformed JSON or an unknown mode is an error, never a silent free.

correctness-57: `CheckPolicy` runs inside `acdsl check` (not as a registry verifier): free mode never diffs; the base is merge-base(HEAD, first resolvable of base_ref, origin/HEAD, origin/main, main, master); HEAD at the base tip passes vacuously; no resolvable base in strict/gated is a hard error (exit 2) naming the fix; runCheck prepends policy diagnostics to verifier diagnostics before logVerdicts and returns exitError on load/check errors.

correctness-58: In strict/gated mode any difference of acdsl/policy.json, policy.schema.json, registry.json or evalgen.json versus the base (absent on one side counts, absent on both is clean) is a violation.
correctness-59: In strict/gated mode every entry name in acdsl/registry.local.json (read directly, tracked or untracked) must appear in `local_overrides`, else a violation.

correctness-60: The rule delta over changed and untracked declaration files classifies added/removed/changed rules (changed = trimmed marker line differs; base side parsed from git show with base authoring violations ignored); strict flags every entry; gated flags entries whose SCOPE segment (non-matching ID = protected) is outside editable_scopes and added/changed entries binding a verifier outside the allowlist (empty = the base-ref registry's names); task-lifetime entries are dropped first when allow_task_contracts is true.

correctness-61: Policy diagnostics carry RuleId `ACDSL-POLICY`, Verifier `policy`, Message `<file>:<line>: policy(<mode>): rule <id> added|modified|removed outside <detail>`, and a Why naming the fix (sanction it on the base ref, or revert).

correctness-62: git.go gains GitMergeBase, GitRevParse (error carries git stderr), GitChangedFiles (diff --name-only <base> merged with untracked non-ignored files) and GitShowFile (absent path → ok=false, no error), all through internal/shell.Run with the context deadline.

correctness-63: `Dist` ships the policy via `writePolicy`: mode rewritten from dist_mode (falling back to the source mode), dist_mode stripped, schema copied verbatim, output line `acdsl/policy.json -> mode: <mode>`; no source policy ships nothing and adds no line.

correctness-64: `cmd/hooks/acdsl-policy-guard.sh` (fail-open when jq is missing, bash 3.2, shellcheck-clean) walks up from cwd to the nearest acdsl/policy.json and in gated/strict denies writes to policy.json, policy.schema.json, registry.json, registry.local.json and evalgen.json, in strict also any *.acdsl or acdsl/* path, using the worktree-write-guard deny JSON shape; paths outside the policy repo pass; it is registered in settings.json's PreToolUse Write|Edit|NotebookEdit hooks after worktree-write-guard (timeout 10); acdsl/README.md gains the Modes section (with permissions.deny snippet and amended registry.local.json paragraph) and docs/acdsl-spec.md a modes paragraph.

correctness-65: The railroad-review lane prompt invokes the Skill tool with skill="railroad-review" and args="--no-context" (CTX-002), and that is the only `no-context` site in railroad-review.js; skill-context.sh and read-gate.sh stay unchanged.

correctness-66: The SKILL.md CTX-002 parenthetical is corrected from 'they never invoke a skill' to the real mechanism (lanes invoke the skill with --no-context; the direction's named entries are the lane's only context).
correctness-67: railroad-review bumps its version 8.2 → 8.3 in frontmatter and changelog.json[0], the entry naming both the context fix and the branch rename.

correctness-68: Branch builders produce `claude-review/{direction}[-{chunkSlug}]-l{i}-r{r}-{hash6}` (lanes), `claude-review/refute-{slug}-r{r}-{hash6}` (refuters) and `claude-review/station-r{r}-{hash6}` (station); the cleanup enumeration derives from the same builders; no `claude/railroad` string remains under skills/quality/railroad-review/.
correctness-69: Every 'claude/* namespace' mention in the lane/refuter/station prompts, cleanup notes and SKILL.md branch-name prose reads 'claude-review/* namespace'.

correctness-70: Trace runbook `plans/railroad-review-observability/runbooks/trace.md` provides jq recipes over on-disk workflow transcripts (lane roster, per-lane context reads vs direction requirements, injection check, per-agent tokens and wall time rolled up per direction/round, step adherence) plus the before/after procedure, with no peek-mcp dependency; an aborted lane shows as aborted rather than crashing a recipe.

correctness-71: Eviction screen recipe `plans/railroad-review-observability/runbooks/eviction-screen.md` takes at least 3 traced runs and flags entries never read by a requiring lane AND never cited AND with enforcement not gate/lint, writing a candidate table with evidence pointers to `evals/railroad-review-<date>/eviction-candidates.md`; nothing is persisted on context entries and removal stays a manual tombstone.

correctness-72: The peek verbose mode is recorded only as a contract (session_agents, session_agent_events with events_only, session_full include_thinking with subagent thinking excluded); nothing in this change implements or depends on it.

correctness-73: The Welcome Bootstrap card becomes a form (hx-post /welcome/bootstrap, hx-confirm kept, hx-disabled-elt on the button) with a native `<input type="date" name="since">` prefilled to today minus 30 days with max today (BootstrapSinceDefault/BootstrapToday computed in the welcome handler, format 2006-01-02) and an optional `extra-prompt` text input (maxlength 500).

correctness-74: smine gains `--since <YYYY-MM-DD>` (argument-hint, Args, §1 Resolve, §2 Run) passed verbatim to smine-batch, and the session-mine.js workflow forwards `args.since`; absent means no date floor.

correctness-75: smine-batch `--since`: sessions whose `last_active` is before the date are dropped before batching (date inclusive) and never listed as skipped; remaining sessions are ordered newest → oldest.

correctness-76: The casual audience value is `casual`: `audienceCasual = "casual"`, `isDeveloperAudience` returns Audience != casual (a legacy `non-developer` value reads as developer), run.sh compares `casual` for the orchestrate/auto-apply defaults, the de profile template writes `audience: casual` with 'casual user' prose, the installer label reads '(German, casual)', and tests/skill prose are renamed; no `non-developer` mode reference remains outside historical dirs.

correctness-77: sync_skills.sh migrates the profile in place (`audience: non-developer` → `audience: casual`, temp file + mv) before reading the audience, leaves any other value untouched, and applies the overrides when the audience is `casual`.

correctness-78: smine-apply (and skillroutine-create when driven by a proposal) stamps `origin: user` in the frontmatter (after `author:`) of every skill created from a proposal; never added to shipped skills, never removed.

correctness-79: Casual lockout: smine-skills drops skill/workflow edit candidates whose target SKILL.md lacks `origin: user` (reported as `dropped: casual lockout — <target>`, never written to skills.json; new-skill proposals still allowed); smine-apply refuses such proposals with disposition `casual-locked` and a note regardless of vote or auto-apply mode; smine-orchestrate rejects any run commit modifying a non-`origin: user` skill on a casual install; all with version bumps.

correctness-80: smine-batch routes each session to `sessions/<roster-name>/` from `--repos` attribution or to `sessions/default/` when unmatched or no roster is given; `batch.scope` carries the folder name; a batch never spans folders; batch numbers continue per folder (a fresh folder starts at 01); the ledger is `sessions/<name>/analyzed-sessions.txt`; the Select skip-list is the union of all live and archived folder ledgers; the schema.json scope description is updated.

correctness-81: `--scopes` is removed from smine, smine-batch, session-mine.js and docs; smine --no-batch cursor resolution enumerates every folder under sessions/ except archived/; smine-skills/context/routines/memory input globs exclude archived/; README and comments describe repo folders + default + archived.

correctness-82: Existing sessions/personal and sessions/work folders are not migrated — they remain ordinary browsable folders until archived via the UI; removing a repo from the registry leaves its sessions folder untouched.

correctness-83: The sessions store skips `sessions/archived/` when enumerating scopes; `ArchiveScope` moves sessions/<name> to sessions/archived/<name> (error if already archived), `UnarchiveScope` moves it back (error and nothing moved if a live folder of that name exists), `DeleteScope` removes only an archived folder (error otherwise), `ArchivedFolders` lists archived folders with md-report counts (missing dir → empty); `validateScopeName` rejects empty, `archived`, `.`, `..` and names containing path separators while `default` stays archivable.

correctness-84: Routes `GET /sessions/archive`, `POST /sessions/{scope}/archive`, `POST /sessions/archive/{name}/unarchive` and `POST /sessions/archive/{name}/delete` are registered; the op handlers render the op-result fragment with any error and set HX-Redirect to /sessions (archive) or /sessions/archive (unarchive/delete).

correctness-85: The Reload button, `POST /sessions/reload` (now 404), `handleSessionsReload`, the `sessions-reload` HX-Trigger wiring and the 'Reload from disk' catalog entry are deleted; `handleSessionsIndex`, `handleSessionsScope`, `handleSessionsBatch`, `handleSessionsArchiveTab` and `handleOverview` call `s.sessions.Reload()` first (error → logged, page still renders) so a batch written while the server runs appears on the next load.

correctness-86: The sessions index gains an archive tab link and an 'Archive folder' button with confirm on the active folder; new `sessions_archive.html` lists archived folders with Unarchive and Delete (confirm naming the re-mining consequence) or 'No archived folders.'; the empty-state index also renders the tabs row; all new strings are in germanCatalog.

correctness-87: The repo add form gets an editable `name` field (default: folder basename); `Repo.Validate` rejects the reserved names `default` and `archived`; duplicate names are still rejected with the existing error; the name is validated before the git-init step so a rejected add never initializes a repo.

correctness-88: New `cmd/bootstrap/run.sh` (bash 3.2, shellcheck-clean) exports MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 and MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*', sources routines/_lib/platform.sh and skill.sh, and preflights: not on main → exit 64, dirty tree → exit 64, missing jq/shellcheck → warning only; a non-dry run requires a non-empty BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_FILE (else exit 78) and exports CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN from it.

correctness-89: run.sh reads language/audience/dev-mode from the profile via sed; dev mode = SMINE_DEV_MODE or profile `dev-mode: true`, forced off for the casual audience; it copies ~/.config/claude-routine/skill-overrides.json into the repo `.claude/settings.local.json` when present (non-dry) and builds `--repos name=path` from git dirs in settings.json additionalDirectories.

correctness-90: Stage prompts: `/smine-style $n`; `/smine --nightly` with `--since <d>` when BOOTSTRAP_SINCE is set else `--last <BOOTSTRAP_N, default 30>`, `--dev` when on, `--repos`, `--agents ${SMINE_AGENTS:-claude,codex}` and the extra prompt appended; consolidate with `language <lang>` when not en; `/smine-apply proposals/<votes file>` with implementation cap, `auto-apply: decide` and the rules file (the empty votes file created first); `/smine-orchestrate bootstrap` plus `(since: <d>)` when set.

correctness-91: Each stage runs via `routine_run_claude` with `--allowedTools` from the installed skill manifest (warning when empty), `--add-dir $HOME/.claude/context/global`, model/effort/permission-mode/budget and JSON output; the envelope is appended to the results JSONL; a failing stage is logged and the run continues, orchestrate always runs last; `BOOTSTRAP_DRY_RUN=1` prints one DRY line per stage and executes nothing.

correctness-92: Wrapper postconditions: a dirty tree after the stages exits 70 with the `.orchestrate-report` tail; otherwise the report file is removed, completion is printed, and the exit status is the first non-zero stage status (0 if none).

correctness-93: bootstrap.go replaces `bootstrapSkillArgs` with `bootstrapEnv(since, extraPrompt)` (YYYY-MM-DD validation, quotes/newlines rejected → 400) returning BOOTSTRAP_SINCE/BOOTSTRAP_EXTRA_PROMPT entries; the handler spawns `exec bash cmd/bootstrap/run.sh` via verifyPathPrefix with those env entries plus BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_FILE (and the routine model/token values); concurrency refusal, 6h deadline, logging and status polling are unchanged.

correctness-94: `skills/smine/smine-bootstrap/` is deleted and its references swept (outside historical dirs) from README, docs, comments and skills indexes; the operator entry `bash cmd/bootstrap/run.sh` with BOOTSTRAP_* env is documented in the script header and README.

correctness-95: smine and smine-batch gain `--last <n>` (applied after the merge/exclusion steps: keep the newest n, drop the rest silently; `--since` wins when both are given) and `--dev`, both passed through verbatim from smine to smine-batch; versions bumped.

correctness-96: The presentation profile gains `DevMode` parsed from `dev-mode:` (true only for the literal `true`); `saveProfileSelection(audience, language, devMode)` writes a `dev-mode: <bool>` front-matter line and deletes the file only when audience/language are default and devMode is false; an `isDevMode()` accessor reads under RLock.

correctness-97: The profile save handler sets dev mode = `dev_mode=on` AND audience not casual; profile.html shows a 'Dev mode — include smine and routine sessions in mining' checkbox, disabled for the casual audience, backed by a `DevMode` page field.

correctness-98: smine-batch Select without `--dev` drops sessions whose cwd resolves inside the run's repo root (including .claude/worktrees/) or whose git_branch starts with `claude-routines/`, reporting a single line `excluded N smine/routine sessions (dev mode off)`; with `--dev` they qualify normally.

correctness-99: The nightly run.sh reads `dev-mode:` (initialized empty with the other profile vars), honors SMINE_DEV_MODE, forces dev mode off for casual, and appends `--dev` to the `/smine --nightly` prompt when on.

correctness-100: smine-style writes its directive lines in the presentation-profile language (absent profile: the dominant language of the sampled user turns), and a write failure on the target path is reported as a stage failure, never staged elsewhere; version bumped.

correctness-101: On casual installs smine-context/memory/routines/skills author user-visible prose (title change-name, change, fields label/text, evidence titles, session notes) without file paths, rule/FACT/ACDSL IDs or schema/taxonomy jargon, keeping technical anchors in target/anchor/code/snippet fields; smine-consolidate §4 sweeps remaining offending prose into the technical fields without deleting content; versions bumped.
